extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and KIPO examiners handling expedited examination, prior-art searches, and pre-appeal reconsideration
extracted.subtask_description: Official Korean Intellectual Property Office examination guidelines describing eligibility, procedural requirements, and evaluation criteria for requests for expedited examination (including prior-art-search based requests, special-project/medical/aged-applicant cases) and for examiner reconsideration prior to appeal proceedings. Covers required documents, timelines, report content, amendment rules, and examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory correspondence explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike any other evidential documents, an explanation on correspondence must be submitted in any case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where differences (between claims etc.) exist they shall be indicated in a written explanation. If explanations are not indicated an examiner may order amendment; explanations may include responses to international opinions or claims that irregularities are addressed through amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling 'opinions on an international application' in Box VIII
rubrics_metrics.description: Where 'opinions on an international application' are indicated in Box No. VIII of an international search/ preliminary search opinion or international preliminary examination report, the intention that all the claims of the concerned patent application are not affected by those opinions shall be explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations may include (i) responses to the international opinions and (ii) claims that irregularities are addressed through amendments. If such explanations are not indicated, an examiner may order amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of determination on expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining expedited examination on a patent application agreed for expedited examination with a foreign patent office, the result of the determination shall not be notified to the requester, except when a request is determined to be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If determination rejects the request, it shall be notified to the requester as with other requests for expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redetermination when amendments occur post-determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant amends a specification or claims after a determination on expedited examination but before examination is initiated, the examiner may instruct corrections to the expedited request and re-determine whether to permit expedited examination considering the corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may grant a correction order designating a period up to one month at his discretion to allow applicant correction prior to re-determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited exam without re-determination when correspondence provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant submits an explanation comparing all claims (including amended ones) with prior art cited in a foreign office notification, or correspondence explanation with claims recognized patentable by a foreign office or by international search/examination, expedited examination shall be conducted without re-determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing full correspondence/explanations that show claims alignment with recognized patentable claims avoids the need for re-determining expedited status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model expedited examination eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for utility model registration requested for examination upon filing and then requested for expedited examination within two months from filing is eligible for expedited examination; patent applications are not eligible under this clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models have 10-year term and tend to be for shorter lifecycle tech; however, divisional/converted utility model applications cannot claim the parent's filing date and cannot be requested for expedited examination based on those requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional/converted utility model ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model application divided or converted from a prior-filed application cannot hold the retrospective filing date of the prior-filed application and cannot be requested for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such divisional or converted utility model applications are not eligible for expedited examination under the stated requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization project related application eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directly related to any specialization project under Article 36-8 of the Act on Special Cases concerning Special Economic Zones is eligible for expedited examination; utility model applications are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic requirements: (i) if jointly filed, one applicant must be recognized by the relevant central administrative agency as a specialization project operator or participant; (ii) applicant must be designated as operator/participant on at least one of filing date, request date, or determination date; (iii) determination of operator can be found in official gazette and supporting documents may be required; (iv) inventions must be directly related to the specialization project — correlation is determined based on the expedited-exam written explanation and the official gazette; examiners may order corrections or may accept eligibility without further investigation if relation is likely and no special grounds exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-tech medical complex R&D application eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directly related to research and development of medical services within the relevant high-tech medical complex filed by a resident research and development institute of medical services under the Special Act is eligible for expedited examination; utility model applications are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic requirements mirror specialization project rules: (i) in joint filings at least one applicant must be a designated resident R&D institute; (ii) designation must hold on filing/request/determination date; (iii) inventions must be directly related to R&D of the medical service; examiners may order corrections to verify correlation or may accept eligibility where relation is likely and no particular grounds exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art search by authorized institute requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester of expedited examination may commission a prior art search to an authorized prior art search institute designated by the Commissioner (e.g., Korea Institute of Patent Information, WIPS Co., IP Solutions); the search results must be submitted to the Commissioner within one month after the request for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent applications whose search results by the authorized institute are required to be notified to the Commissioner shall be eligible. If the authorized institute fails to submit the report within one month, the examiner shall issue a correction order. The failure or deficiency triggers correction orders; uncorrected deficiencies can lead to rejection of the expedited request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination when search report from authorized institute is submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications whose search report is submitted by an authorized prior art search institute, the examiner shall make a determination on expedited examination; where the claims to be examined are identical with the claims in the prior art search report, a request for expedited examination shall be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the search report does not meet the guideline for writing reports (see below) and cannot be used, the examiner shall make a correction order within the designated period and may reject the expedited request if not corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written request requirements when prior art search commissioned
rubrics_metrics.description: A written explanation of a request for expedited examination shall be attached. However, when prior art search is requested to a specialized/authorized institute and the application is marked accordingly, submission of a written request including the institute name and date of request suffices and no additional written request is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the written expedited request omits the date and name of the search institute, the examiner must undertake designation procedures and may require corrected documents that include them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications relying on parent search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is determined on a parent application based on an authorized prior art search report and all claims of a divisional application in the parent's search report have already been examined, a request for expedited examination for the divisional can be filed without an additional prior art search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should submit a contrastive explanation indicating all claims of the divisional are identical with the parent's pre-division claims and a written explanation that the prior art search results for the divisional are included in the parent's report. If examiner finds search results on divisional claims are not indicated, a correction order will be issued; failure to correct can lead to rejection of the expedited request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of prior art documents in search report
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, more than five prior art documents shall be included in a prior art search report for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no close or relevant prior art exists (e.g., new technical field), the reasons for fewer documents must be stated; indication of fewer than four documents may be allowed with grounds. Refer to paragraph (2)(c) of instructions for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search result content requirements in search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report must indicate, for each searched prior art document, the problems solved by that document compared with all claims and the means for solving those problems, with concerned pages and lines indicated; contents related to the claimed invention shall be written consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claims related to the claimed invention must be indicated in the box for 'Relevant Claims' in the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrastive explanation requirements in search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Similarities and differences with the closest prior art document shall be separately described claim-by-claim in detail, with prior art content indicated in detail (pages/lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the closest prior art for each claim and explain similarities/differences; each claim does not need to be compared with all listed prior art documents. In principle, contrastive explanation shall cover all claims, but independent claims that differ only in dependent claims and categories may be grouped. If novelty/inventive step is recognized in independent claims (relevance marked 'A'), a brief contrastive explanation for dependent claims may suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling amended specifications after prior-art search request
rubrics_metrics.description: If prior art search was commissioned and the specification was later amended before filing the request for expedited examination (so the search was conducted on pre-amended claims), and then a search report is re-submitted at time of filing a request after a correction order, the examiner shall make a determination on expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where grounds for request change due to prior art search after correction order, the examiner decides on legitimacy of the ground for change. Applicants must indicate date of request for prior art search and name of the authorized institute in corrected documents so the examiner can designate the search institution and upload the report. Prior art search reports for expedited examination are due within one month (super-expedited: 10 days); failure to submit within time after correction orders triggers further correction orders and potential rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for submission of prior art search reports
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, a prior art search report for expedited examination shall be submitted within one month from the date of the request (super-expedited: within 10 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not submitted by the time examiner decides on expedited examination following a correction period, the examiner shall issue another correction order and non-submission can lead to rejection of the expedited request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aged or terminally ill applicant expedited eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application filed by a person over 65 or a terminally ill patient may be eligible for expedited examination because they may not be able to take steps up to final disposal without expedited proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over 65 is treated as aged. Terminal illness is determined based on diagnosis or doctor's note per Article 3 of the Medical Act; the criterion is whether the applicant's health prevents taking examination steps, not the specific disease name or seriousness. Examples of acceptable doctor statements are provided indicating limited remaining lifespan or inability to follow procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration before appeal: initiation and legal basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person who received a decision to reject has submitted a notice of appeal and made an amendment in the specification or drawings within thirty days after submission of the notice, the IPTAB notifies the Commissioner, who shall have the examiner reexamine the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions of Articles 51, 57(2), 78 and parts of 148 apply mutatis mutandis to the reexamination under Article 173. Other articles apply in specified ways where grounds for rejection differ or notice of appeal is deemed reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes of reexamination before appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If grounds for decision to reject are resolved as a result of reexamination, the examiner shall reverse the decision to reject and make a decision to grant a patent; the notice of appeal is deemed extinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner cannot grant a patent after reexamination, he shall report the result to the Commissioner, who will notify the President of the IPTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for reconsideration by examiners prior to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Only patent applications subject to a decision to reject may be reconsidered prior to appeal. The appellant must submit a notice of appeal within 30 days of receiving the certified copy of the decision and must amend the specification or drawings within 30 days from filing the appeal; even formal (non-substantive) amendments are subject to reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application was invalidated or returned rather than rejected, it is not eligible for reconsideration under this procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities and assignment for pre-appeal reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of notification that a notice of appeal was filed, the trial policy division completes formality examination and forwards the case to the patent examination bureau; the director registers the case and hands it to an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle the examiner who made the decision to reject should re-examine, but if that examiner moved divisions or it's improper another suitable examiner may re-examine. Defective notices of appeal should, in principle, be remanded to the IPTAB unless defects are minor and easily rectified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of amendments during reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made within 30 days from filing an appeal shall correspond to those necessitated by the final rejection and must be within the scope of the matters described in the originally filed specification or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of claim amendments within 30 days is limited to: (1) narrowing the scope by restricting or deleting a claim or adding an element; (2) correcting clerical errors; (3) clarifying ambiguous description; (4) reinstating claims before amendment or certain amendments in accordance with Article 47(3) exceptions. Criteria for evaluating scope/requirements of amendments refer to Chapter 2 of Part 4 of the Examination Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendments that are illegitimate
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment within 30 days may be refused entry if it does not comply with requirements under Article 47(2)-(3) or if the amendment gives rise to new grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If previously notified grounds for rejection are not overcome by the amendment but no new grounds arise, the amendment may be accepted but the original decision stands. If new grounds arise from the amendment, the amendment shall be refused entry and review proceeds based on the pre-amendment specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison baseline for evaluating successive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline for evaluating whether an amendment introduces new matter or narrows scope depends on the procedural history (e.g., amendment I/II/III/IV); comparisons use either the originally filed application or the most recently entered amendment depending on circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (i) If decision to reject came after notice of non-final rejection based on amendment II and applicant files amendment III with appeal, new matter (Article 47(2)) is compared to the originally filed specification, while Article 47(3) amendment requirements are evaluated against amendment II — scope narrowing is determined by comparing corresponding claims between amendment II and amendment III. Similar comparison rules apply for other scenarios (decision after final rejection, refusal to enter amendment, etc.).
